title: Renewal Terms of Your HomeGuard Homeowners Policy
content:
Each HomeGuard Homeowners Policy term runs twelve calendar months. These terms state when a policy renews, what changes at renewal, and when a renewal payment received after the expiration date is still accepted.

## 1. The renewal offer

A policy that is in force and not under a notice of nonrenewal is offered renewal. Installment 1 of the renewal term is billed the package's renewal offer lead days before the expiration date, at the renewal term premium produced by the rating system. That renewal term premium becomes the policy's term premium when the policy renews.

## 2. Renewal on the expiration date

The policy renews on its expiration date for a new term of twelve calendar months when renewal installment 1 was paid in full on or before the expiration date. A mortgagee-billed policy renews on its mortgagee invoice.

At renewal:

- **Coverage A** becomes the expiring Coverage A increased by the package's inflation guard percentage, rounded up to the next 1000 USD, and capped at the package's maximum Coverage A.
- **Roof settlement basis** is re-evaluated on the roof age at the new effective date, by the same test applied when a policy is bound.
- **EFT suspension**, where it was set during the expiring term, resets so that the policy is no longer suspended.

*Hypothetical worked figures.* With an inflation guard of 4 percent: an expiring Coverage A of 312300 USD increased by 4 percent is 324792 USD, which rounds up to 325000 USD. With a package maximum of 450000 USD, an expiring Coverage A of 440000 USD increased by 4 percent is 457600 USD, rounded up to 458000 USD and capped at 450000 USD.

## 3. When the renewal installment is not paid

When renewal installment 1 is still unpaid at the end of the expiration date, the policy expires with the recorded reason that the renewal was not paid.

## 4. Late renewal payment

A late renewal payment is accepted only when it is received no later than the late-payment window that starts on the expiration date.

| Element | Basis |
|---|---|
| Date the window starts from | The expiration date on the policy record |
| Unit | Calendar days |
| Last day of the window | The expiration date plus the package's renewal late-payment days |
| Payment received on the last day | Accepted |

A policy renewed this way renews **with a lapse**: the new term starts on the day the payment is received, there is no coverage between the expiration date and that day, and the new expiration date is twelve calendar months after the new effective date.

A policy that expired under a notice of nonrenewal can never be renewed late, whatever the date of the payment.

### Boundary cases (hypothetical)

Hypothetical inputs: an expiration date of 1 June and a late-payment window of 30 days, so the last day is 1 July.

| Payment received | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 July, policy expired for non-payment of the renewal | Accepted; new term from 1 July, no coverage from 1 June to 1 July, new expiration 1 July of the following year |
| 2 July | Not accepted |
| 20 June, policy expired under a notice of nonrenewal | Not accepted |
